title: A ticket's cursor crosses through one command
intention: A ticket's cursor crosses through one command that calls transitions.emit at the ticket's own component and writes the moved cursor back onto the ticket in the same act, so no voyage needs an ad hoc script to cross.
why: Peer F21 (2026-10-07): there is no CLI crossing door, so every voyage crosses through an ad hoc script that calls emit. F32 (2026-10-08) cast it next, with this measured divergence as its why: 4784351e4838's rehearsal, CLEAN before decide line D11, then raised 3, 2, 1, 4 and 9 gaps over five passes after D11-D15 — every gap on crossing machinery (emit, clear, write_verdict, predict, lacks), never on the build — and went CLEAN in one pass only once D16 ruled crossings outside a ticket's build scope. Series: CLEAN -> 3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 9 -> CLEAN. Spend: 10 passes, $3.74, $1.98 of it the diverged five. A crossing with no standing command is machinery each ticket re-describes, and the reader treats named machinery as scope (80518446bfc8, n=1). Under RULE 1 the command berths where emit lives.
traces_to: Law 1 (a crossing is a settled act; re-deriving its script per voyage spends the resolver on the settled) and RULE 1 (crossings belong to the workflow's own component, tools/base where emit lives, not to each ticket's build or rehearsal — F32).
how: cairn/tools/base/cross.py beside cast.py: python3 -m cairn.tools.base.cross <ticket-id> <TARGET> --actor <who> --why <why> [--proven-by P ...] [--missing M ...]. It resolves the ticket in the store transitions already names (_TICKETS, overridable for a proof as cast_ticket's tickets_dir is), derives the component from the ticket's owning_intention (the charter's directory; refuses one that carries no charter), calls emit with history/state at that component and ticket=<id>, and on success writes the rendered cursor into workflow_and_state through the artifact door (verb cast). A refusal from emit prints verbatim and writes nothing. The crossing into a rest (PROVED) is refused by name: it belongs to harbor_master's clearance, a device-held machine this tool may not reach (RULE 1).
